title: Stock order matching
brief: Brokers and traders send buy and sell orders, and you pair them fairly: the earliest order at the best price goes first. At the market open a rush of orders arrives in seconds. Every accepted order must be in one agreed sequence, and no trade may be lost or invented.

clarify.q: Who decides the order of two orders sent at the same instant?
clarify.a: One sequencer. Everything downstream follows its log, and that log is the truth.

clarify.q: Can we lose an order we already acknowledged?
clarify.a: Never. The acknowledgement means the order is safely in the sequence.

clarify.q: What if the network splits in two?
clarify.a: It is better to stop trading on the smaller side than to let two sides disagree about trades.
Quotes are copies. A quote a few seconds old is fine for a portfolio screen, not for matching.

notes: Orders and cancels are both writes.

hints: Two machines cannot both decide who was first. What single thing can hold the agreed order?
An ordered, replicated log (a stream) is the sequencer. Matching workers read it in order and write trades to a strongly consistent store.
A retry cannot create another order or change its priority. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: Order and speed meet in one idea: an ordered log. Every order is appended to a replicated stream, and the append is the acknowledgement. Matching workers read the log in order and write trades to a store that refuses to disagree with itself (consensus), so a partition makes the smaller side stop instead of splitting the truth. The opening rush arrives in seconds, which is far faster than autoscaling reacts, so capacity is bought in advance.

designs.name: Sequencer log, matching workers, consensus store
designs.why: Orders are acknowledged as soon as they are in the replicated log. Matching reads the log in order. Quotes come from a cache so portfolio screens never touch the matching path.

tradeoffs: An ordered log gives one agreed sequence and an audit trail for free. The cost is that one partition handles one stream of orders at a time, so orders are split by instrument, not shuffled.
Acknowledging at the log means the sender hears "accepted" before the trade is matched. That is how real exchanges work: accepted is not the same as filled.
A consensus store halts the smaller side of a partition. Trading pauses for a few minutes instead of two sides inventing different trades.
Paying for the opening-rush capacity all day costs real money. The alternative, autoscaling, adds servers minutes after the rush has already failed.
Quotes from a cache are a few seconds old, which is fine for a portfolio and wrong for a matching decision. The matching path never reads the cache.
editorial.realWorld: Large exchanges handle millions of messages a second (orders, cancels and quote updates) at their busiest, using a single ordered log per market and recovering from replicas of that log (approx.).

correctness.prompt: Stock order matching: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Preserve price-time priority through leader failure and order retries. Price-time priority requires one agreed sequence, not scheduling luck. Fencing prevents split-brain trades; replay reconstructs deterministic book state. A retry cannot create another order or change its priority.

fields.label: Step 1. Buy orders A and B have the same price; A was committed first. Who matches first?
options: A using the authoritative sequenced log
fields.explanation: Price-time priority requires one agreed sequence, not scheduling luck.

fields.label: Step 2. A new leader takes over while the old one is paused. What protects trades?
options: Let both match until their clocks agree
Fence the old leader and replay committed orders before matching
fields.explanation: Fencing prevents split-brain trades; replay reconstructs deterministic book state.

fields.label: Step 3. An accepted order retries after a lost reply. What is appended?
options: Append a new order at the new arrival time
Return the existing order id and sequence
fields.explanation: A retry cannot create another order or change its priority.

correctness.responsibility: Preserve price-time priority through leader failure and order retries.
correctness.limits: The traffic model does not execute this protocol. The checked trace covers its central responsibility; the written explanation is retained for review.

twist.brief: Demand has settled at about 2500 requests/s. The new monthly ceiling is $20412. The original burst reserve now competes with the operating budget. Decide which reserve to keep, then test its failure headroom. All data and recovery promises still apply.

design.name: Smaller workload, measured reserve
design.why: Reduce the paid floor for the quieter workload, preserving the required copies and recovery settings. This design was checked through the full event day.
